name: WeWork KABUTO ONE
card: Floors 9–10 of a redevelopment in Kabutocho's financial district, connected to Kayabacho Station
title: WeWork KABUTO ONE — a site at the heart of Kabutocho's redevelopment, directly connected to Kayabacho Station
lead: WeWork KABUTO ONE is on the 9th and 10th floors of KABUTO ONE, at the centre of Nihonbashi Kabutocho, which is being redeveloped as a National Strategic Special Zone project for the Tokyo area. It is directly connected to Kayabacho Station on the subway, and an underground passage leads to Nihombashi Station. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Completed August 2021 / 15 floors above ground, 2 below
Ceiling height 2,800 mm / 15 meeting rooms / phone booths and more
hero_cap: The 9th-floor entrance of WeWork KABUTO ONE
concept: Fit for Kabutocho, the international financial district
With meeting rooms of all sizes and phone booths, the site was designed for practical office use and the functionality befitting Kabutocho as an international financial district, the website says.
The building also has a hall, library and lounge where local companies can mix — a site where you feel both the energy of the redevelopment and the energy of the WeWork community.
steps: You enter the site on the 9th floor.
Straight ahead is the community bar, which doubles as reception and a place to mingle.
By the windows on the 9th and 10th floors
Both the 9th and 10th floors have window-side lounges.
By the windows of the 9th-floor lounge
By the windows of the 10th-floor lounge
There are 15 meeting rooms, and the website says it can accommodate private offices and custom requests.

word.title: What is a National Strategic Special Zone?
body: A system in which the national government designates areas and eases regulations to boost economic growth and international competitiveness.
The Tokyo area is one, and the redevelopment of Kabutocho is proceeding as one of its projects.

name: WeWork Jimbocho
card: Hand-drawn art inspired by the book town — small and homely
title: WeWork Jimbocho — a small site with hand-drawn art from the book town, 2 minutes from Jimbocho Station
lead: WeWork Jimbocho is a two-minute walk from Jimbocho Station on the subway. Seven stations are within reach, and the area combines educational and cultural institutions with a busy shopping district. The website highlights the homely community of a small site and hand-drawn art inspired by the book town. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Completed November 2011 / 8 floors above ground, 1 below
Ceiling height 2,900 mm / 5 meeting rooms / phone booths, parents' room, honesty market and more
concept: Art born from the book town
The shared areas have hand-drawn art created with inspiration from Jimbocho, famous as Tokyo's book town. Art is woven into the lounges and private offices too, the website says.
Small as it is, it packs WeWork's functionality and comfort into one site.
steps: Hand-drawn art inspired by Jimbocho brightens the shared areas.
A small site means a homely community.
Art is also brought into the private offices to create spaces where it is easy to focus, the website says.
There are five meeting rooms, plus phone booths, a parents' room and an honesty market.
With seven stations nearby, getting around central Tokyo is quick.

word.title: What is a parents' room?
body: A private room where members with children can nurse, change nappies or take a break.
Many WeWork sites have one — part of making it easier to work while raising children.

name: THE HUB Shiodome
card: A whole building in Shiodome's “Italian Quarter”, with a lounge and reception rooms
title: THE HUB Shiodome — rental offices and coworking across a whole building in the Italian Quarter, Showa Astec Building No. 1
lead: THE HUB Shiodome is in Showa Astec Building No. 1 in Shiodome's “Italian Quarter” business area, a seven-minute walk from exit A2 of Daimon Station on the Toei Oedo Line and eight from the Karasumori exit of Shimbashi Station. The website describes “a wide range of sizes only a whole building can offer, plus generous shared spaces”. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Reinforced concrete (SRC on the ground floor), 7 floors; renovated March 2017
Private offices / lounge / waiting space / meeting room / reception room / booth seats
Rental office from ¥65,289/month / all-site plan ¥16,500/month / single-site plan ¥8,800/month
concept: The breadth of a whole building
The website introduces it as “a rental office and coworking space in Shiodome's Italian Quarter business area”.

Using an entire seven-storey building, it offers many room sizes and generous shared spaces such as a lounge and reception room. It is seven minutes from Daimon, eight from Shimbashi and nine from the North Exit of Hamamatsucho.
steps: A whole building in the Italian Quarter
Showa Astec Building No. 1 is a seven-storey building renovated in March 2017.
Visitors can wait in the waiting space.
The lounge is open to tenants and coworking members: the all-site plan is ¥16,500 a month, the single-site plan ¥8,800 and the 10-hour plan ¥2,200.
Drop-in is charged by usage, from ¥275 per 30 minutes.
03 · Meeting room, reception room and booths
Besides a meeting room there is a reception room, so meetings and receiving guests can be kept separate.
Booth seats suit calls, online meetings and focused time.

word.title: What is the Italian Quarter?
body: The name for the blocks around Higashi-Shimbashi 2-chome on the west side of Shiodome. The website describes THE HUB Shiodome as being in “Shiodome's Italian Quarter business area”.
Tucked just behind Shiodome's towers, it is within walking distance of Shimbashi, Hamamatsucho and Daimon stations.

credits: THE HUB official website: “THE HUB Shiodome”

name: THE HUB Takanawa
card: Floors 8–9 of the Grace Takanawa Building, 4 minutes from Sengakuji Station
title: THE HUB Takanawa — a shared office in Takanawa where progress meets calm, on the 8th and 9th floors of the Grace Takanawa Building
lead: THE HUB Takanawa is on the 8th and 9th floors of the Grace Takanawa Building, four minutes from exit A2 of Sengakuji Station on the Toei Asakusa Line and six from Takanawa Gateway Station. The website calls it “a shared office in Takanawa where progress and calm come together”. It has private offices for 2–5, a meeting room for 4, and private and semi-private booth seats. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Steel-reinforced concrete, 11 floors above ground, 1 below
Private offices (2–5 people) / meeting room (4) / booth seats (private and semi-private) / waiting space
concept: Progress and calm
The website introduces it as “a shared office in Takanawa where progress and calm come together”.
Four minutes from Sengakuji, six from Takanawa Gateway and nine from Shinagawa, it sits between the growing new district of Takanawa Gateway and Takanawa's quiet residential streets.
steps: There is a reception terminal, and visitors can wait in the waiting space.
Free drinks, a copier, dedicated mailboxes and parcel lockers, and lockers are available.
A meeting room and seats to retreat to
There is a meeting room for four.
Booth seats come in private and semi-private types, for calls, online meetings or focused time.
Private offices are for 2 to 5 people (currently shown as full on the official site).
Coworking is available from ¥7,150 a month on the single-site plan and ¥2,200 on the 10-hour plan.

word.title: What is a semi-private booth?
body: A seat surrounded by partitions but not fully closed. THE HUB Takanawa has both private and semi-private booth seats.
You can focus without feeling watched, and it is easier to use than a private room.

credits: THE HUB official website: “THE HUB Takanawa”

name: The Executive Centre Kyobashi Edogrand
card: A 26th-floor barista bar overlooking Tokyo Station, connected to Kyobashi Station
title: The Executive Centre Kyobashi Edogrand — a stone-topped barista bar and lounge on the 26th floor, connected to Kyobashi Station
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 26th floor of Kyobashi Edogrand, connected underground to Kyobashi Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line. Tokyo Station is also within walking distance. There is a barista bar with a stone counter, a business lounge furnished by Timothy Oulton, and four meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Connected underground to Kyobashi Sta.; Tokyo, Takaracho and Ginza-itchome stations within walking distance
Private offices / coworking / 4 meeting rooms / members' lounge / call rooms
concept: A 26th floor overlooking Tokyo Station
The website calls Kyobashi Edogrand “an impressive building connected underground to Kyobashi Station” and highlights the views over Tokyo Station.
It is close to Marunouchi, Ginza and Nihonbashi alike. A stone-topped barista bar, a lounge furnished by Timothy Oulton, Herman Miller chairs and height-adjustable desks are all here.
steps: Seats to work and rooms to call
Coworking passes start at ¥54,000 a month and day passes at ¥5,000 a day.
Phone booths along the corridor are for calls and online meetings.
Rooms for teams and four meeting rooms
Private offices are priced on request. The four meeting rooms have pull-down presentation screens and audiovisual equipment.
Outside the windows, the streets around Tokyo Station spread out.

word.title: What is a day office?
body: A plan at The Executive Centre for using a private office during the daytime. At Kyobashi Edogrand it starts at ¥45,000 per person per month.
It suits people who want a private office for set hours before committing to a permanent one.

credits: The Executive Centre official website: “Kyobashi Edogrand”

name: The Executive Centre GranTokyo South Tower
card: 7th floor of a 42-storey tower above the Yaesu South exit, one minute from Tokyo Station
title: The Executive Centre GranTokyo South Tower — serviced offices on the 7th floor, above Tokyo Station's Yaesu South exit
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 7th floor of GranTokyo South Tower, a 42-storey building above the Yaesu South exit, one minute's walk from JR Tokyo Station. The website highlights views of Tokyo Station, the Imperial Palace and the city, abundant natural light and refined interiors. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre GranTokyo South Tower
A 42-storey mixed-use building above the Yaesu South exit of Tokyo Station; 1 min from Tokyo Sta.
Private offices / coworking / meeting rooms / members' lounge / pantry / phone booths
concept: A Yaesu landmark
The website calls GranTokyo South Tower “a 42-storey landmark rising above the Yaesu South exit of Tokyo Station”.

One minute from Tokyo Station and close to Tokyo International Forum, it is in the Yaesu business district. Views of the station, the Imperial Palace and the city, plenty of natural light and refined interiors are its features.
steps: A place for drinks and seats to work
The pantry is where you make drinks.
Height-adjustable desks let you work sitting or standing.
Rooms for teams and for meetings
Private offices can be rented to suit your headcount, and there are private phone booths.
From the meeting-room windows you can see the streets around Tokyo Station.

word.title: What is a business concierge?
body: A staff member at reception who guides visitors, receives mail and arranges meeting rooms. Every Executive Centre has them.
Even a small company can welcome visitors the way a large corporation does.

credits: © The Executive Centre (official website “GranTokyo South Tower”)
The Executive Centre official website: “GranTokyo South Tower”

name: The Executive Centre TOFROM YAESU TOWER
card: Washi lighting, a pine tree and a barista bar inspired by roof tiles
title: The Executive Centre TOFROM YAESU TOWER — 220 seats with Japanese design touches, on the 11th floor connected underground to Tokyo Station
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 11th floor of TOFROM YAESU TOWER, linked to Tokyo Station through the Yaesu underground mall. It has 220 workstations. The website describes an interior with Japanese design elements: a wall of washi-paper lighting, stone paving inspired by the Nakasendo highway, a large pine tree and a barista bar inspired by roof tiles. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre TOFROM YAESU TOWER
A Grade-A office building with environmental certification; connected to Tokyo Station via the Yaesu underground mall
220 workstations / private offices / coworking library / meeting rooms / event space / members' lounge
hero_cap: A meeting room with natural light
concept: An interior with Japanese design touches

The website lists the Japanese design elements in the interior: a wall of washi-paper lighting, stone paving inspired by the Nakasendo highway, a large pine tree and a barista bar inspired by roof tiles.
The building stands at the heart of Yaesu's redevelopment, connected underground to Tokyo Station and three minutes from Nihombashi Station. With 220 workstations, it is a large centre.
steps: A counter inspired by roof tiles
The barista bar, inspired by traditional roof tiles, is the face of the centre.
The members' lounge looks out over Yaesu.
02 · Coworking, private offices and meeting rooms
Seats to work and rooms for teams
There are coworking seats and a library, with height-adjustable desks.
Private offices start from one person, and meeting rooms are filled with natural light.
A meeting room with natural light

word.title: What is the Nakasendo?
body: An Edo-period highway that ran inland from Nihonbashi in Edo to Sanjo Ohashi bridge in Kyoto. Its starting point, Nihonbashi, is right next to Yaesu.
According to the website, the centre has stone paving inspired by the Nakasendo, bringing the area's history into the interior.

credits: © The Executive Centre (official website “TOFROM YAESU TOWER”)
The Executive Centre official website: “TOFROM YAESU TOWER”

name: The Executive Centre World Trade Center South Tower
card: A 17th floor overlooking Tokyo Bay, with a black-marble barista bar, connected to Hamamatsucho Station
title: The Executive Centre World Trade Center Building South Tower — a lounge overlooking Tokyo Bay on the 17th floor, connected to Hamamatsucho Station
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 17th floor of the World Trade Center Building South Tower, directly connected to JR Hamamatsucho Station — a symbol of Hamamatsucho's redevelopment. Floor-to-ceiling windows look out over Tokyo Bay, and the lounge has stone floors, a black-marble barista bar and vintage furniture by Timothy Oulton. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre World Trade Center Building South Tower
Directly connected to Hamamatsucho Sta.; an office building symbolising Hamamatsucho's redevelopment
Private offices / coworking library / 5 meeting rooms / event space / members' lounge
concept: A 17th floor overlooking Tokyo Bay
The website presents the building as a symbol of Hamamatsucho's redevelopment, part of a plan to create “an iconic international business hub for Tokyo”.
The centre is on the 17th floor overlooking Tokyo Bay, with floor-to-ceiling windows, stone floors, a black-marble barista bar and vintage furniture by Timothy Oulton.
steps: A place to welcome visitors and a home for members
A business concierge is at reception, which leads into a spacious lounge with a black-marble barista bar.
Coworking passes start at ¥54,000 a month and day passes at ¥5,000 a day.
There are height-adjustable desks and a coworking library.
Rooms for teams and five meeting rooms
Private offices include sea-facing rooms, and day offices start at ¥45,000 per person per month.

word.title: What is the Asian Headquarters Special Zone?
body: An area designated by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government to attract foreign companies' Asian headquarters and R&D centres to Tokyo.
The website notes that the centre is inside this zone — a location chosen with overseas companies setting up in Japan in mind.

credits: © The Executive Centre (official website “World Trade Center Building South Tower”)
The Executive Centre official website: “World Trade Center Building South Tower”

name: The Collective GranTokyo South Tower
card: JustCo's top-tier brand, on the 9th floor connected to Tokyo Station
title: The Collective GranTokyo South Tower — luxury coworking from JustCo's top-tier brand, directly connected to Tokyo Station
lead: The Collective GranTokyo South Tower is on the 9th floor of GranTokyo South Tower, a complex directly connected to Tokyo Station. It is luxury coworking and shared offices from “The Collective”, JustCo's top-tier brand. It offers Herman Miller Aeron chairs and height-adjustable desks, TWG tea and % Arabica coffee, daily breakfast and a dedicated concierge service. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Shared desks / private offices / multipurpose meeting rooms (small, medium, large) / private meeting room and tea area
concept: A premium experience, meticulous care
The website presents it as luxury coworking and shared offices under “The Collective”, JustCo's top brand, with the headline “A premium experience, meticulous care”.
JustCo GranTokyo South Tower is on the 11th floor of the same building; here on the 9th, breakfast, drinks hours and a dedicated concierge offer a step-up experience.
steps: Shared desks come with Herman Miller Aeron chairs and height-adjustable desks.
Switch between sitting and standing as you work.
The pantry stocks TWG tea and % Arabica coffee. There is breakfast every day and a drinks hour.
A dedicated concierge service handles visitors and arrangements.
Multipurpose rooms in small, medium and large
There are multipurpose meeting rooms in small, medium and large sizes, plus a private meeting room and tea area.
Connected to the Yaesu South exit of Tokyo Station, it suits meetings with people arriving by shinkansen.
You can rent team spaces with independent access control.
From small rooms to suites for whole company teams.

word.title: What is a concierge?
body: A person who takes on users' requests and arrangements — a role best known from hotels.
The Collective GranTokyo South Tower offers a dedicated concierge service.

credits: JustCo official website: “The Collective GranTokyo South Tower”
